concepts.term: Logging linked to the RTC's seconds
concepts.definition: A row is produced when the RTC's unixtime value divides exactly by the interval; that way the times always come out in the same steps, independent of millis() drift.
concepts.example: When unixtime % 10 == 0, the rows 08:30:10, 08:30:20, 08:30:30 are produced.
concepts.pitfall: Waiting for the logging interval with delay(); the button and the screen freeze during that time.

concepts.definition: The number of seconds since 1970; it expresses the time as a single number.
concepts.example: The condition u % 10 == 0 catches every moment whose seconds divide by 10.
concepts.pitfall: Using the seconds value (0-59) on its own; if the interval does not divide 60 (such as 7), uneven steps come out at the change of minute.

concepts.definition: A variable that keeps the second in which the last row was written; it blocks a second row in the same second.
concepts.example: The condition u != sonKayit makes a row print on only one of the five 200 ms passes.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting the flag: a row with the same timestamp comes out on every 200 ms pass.

concepts.definition: Flips a state variable at the moment the button is pressed (the change from "not pressed" to "pressed").
concepts.example: kayitAcik = !kayitAcik; logging switches off when it is on, and on when it is off.
concepts.pitfall: Flipping the state on every pass for as long as the button is held: logging switches on and off out of control.

concepts.definition: Even if the reading fails, the timestamp is written and the sensor fields stay empty; the device keeps running.
concepts.example: If the DHT's DATA wire comes out, the row is written as 2026-01-01 00:00:20,,
concepts.pitfall: Stopping the program when a reading fails (while(true) {}), or not writing the row at all.

concepts.definition: Building the row and writing the row somewhere are in separate functions; when the place written to changes, the row format does not.
concepts.example: When moving from the Serial version to the SD version, only SD writing is added inside kaydet().
concepts.pitfall: Copying the formatting separately for each place it is written; different rows come out in the two places.

quiz.prompt: The logger writes a row every 10 seconds and runs without stopping. How many data rows are written in 1 hour?
quiz.explanation: One hour is 3600 seconds. 3600 ÷ 10 = 360 rows. This calculation is used to estimate how long the card will take to fill up and to choose the logging interval.

quiz.prompt: If KAYIT_ARALIGI is set to 20, at which seconds of the minute are rows produced in this logging logic linked to the RTC's seconds (unixtime % 20 == 0)?
quiz.explanation: 60 seconds divide exactly by 20; that is why the same three seconds come up every minute: 0, 20 and 40 (such as 08:30:20, 08:30:40, 08:31:00). 0 and 30 would be an interval of 30 seconds; 10, 30, 50 are not seconds that divide by 20.

options: Serial.println should be called instead of satirOlustur
The u != sonKayit check is missing; all five passes within the same second meet the condition
quiz.explanation: When the RTC's seconds divide by 20, that second lasts 1000 ms, and the 200 ms passes find the condition true 5 times in that time. A flag such as u != sonKayit makes the row print once in the same second. The other changes do not stop the repeats.

quiz.prompt: Why is waiting for the logging interval with delay(10000) a bad idea in this project?
options: For 10 seconds the button is not read and the screen is not updated; the device does not respond
delay() only works up to 1000 ms
The RTC resets during this time
quiz.explanation: delay() stops the program: even if the button is pressed, it is not noticed, and the time on the LCD freezes. The fix is a non-blocking check with the RTC's seconds or millis() (lesson 27). delay() is not limited to 1000 ms; the RTC and the CSV row are not affected either.

quiz.prompt: While the logger is running, the DHT22's DATA wire comes out and the reading returns NaN. With the design in the lesson, what appears in the log file?
options: The timestamp is written, and the temperature and humidity columns are left empty
The device stops and no rows are written
0 is written in the temperature column
The previous measurement is repeated as it was
quiz.explanation: satirOlustur does not write a field that comes in as NaN and leaves it empty: a row such as 2026-03-14 08:30:20,, comes out. That way the log shows why the measurement is missing, and the columns do not shift. Writing zero would be confused with a real 0 °C measurement.
